title: XorDDoS_Incident_Response_Scenario_974
description: Investigate and respond to a potential security incident involving the Linux/XorDDoS malware on a victim host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has exhibited unusual behavior, including unexpected outbound network connections and suspicious scheduled tasks. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential security incident involving the Linux/XorDDoS malware.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
levels.local_content:

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the victim host for unauthorized or suspicious services that may indicate malware activity.
levels.solution: Check running services and their associated processes to identify any anomalies. The service name associated with the malware's persistence mechanism is network-diagnostics.service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and their associated processes to identify any anomalies.

levels.title: Identify Scheduled Tasks
levels.content: Determine if any scheduled tasks or timers are responsible for automatically executing the malware on the victim host.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd timers and services to find any suspicious scheduled tasks. The name of the timer or task responsible for the malware's execution is network-diagnostics.timer.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd timers and services to find any suspicious scheduled tasks.

levels.title: Identify Reverse Shell Component
levels.content: Identify the component responsible for providing unauthorized remote shell access to the victim host.
levels.solution: Look for scripts or services that establish connections to external hosts on unusual ports. The script name or service responsible for the reverse shell functionality is /usr/local/lib/.netd/revshell.sh.
